subject: Re: PoC / Trial plan — Deployment mode discussion (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: PoC follow-up: deployment mode & next steps

Hi Alice —

Great to speak this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and can put together a concise PoC/trial plan: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Primary goal: validate low-latency inference for ACME search assistants and recommendations (priority).
- Data sensitivity: some PII in logs; ACME requires data isolation and optional in-region hosting.
- Traffic profile: bursty e-commerce traffic, peak ~200 rps, steady ~30 rps.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + customer-supplied questionnaire (security team will review).

Deployment mode options discussed:
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — good for quick validation but may not meet your data isolation preferences.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) — predictable throughput & tenant isolation; sounds like a strong candidate for your throughput + security needs.
- Private VPC / on-prem — we can support for regulated workloads; longer lead time for networking and approval.

Proposed next steps (PoC / trial plan):
1) Confirm target deployment mode (we heard Dedicated capacity as first choice).
2) Agree success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost/unit, model quality).
3) Schedule kickoff with your SRE and security stakeholders; Redwood will assign a technical lead (Ben) and an infra contact.
4) Deliver PoC plan and timeline (attached draft).

Can you confirm: 1) Dedicated capacity is still preferred, and 2) who from ACME do we include on the kickoff (SRE lead, security, procurement)? Also attaching a short draft PoC plan and our standard security questionnaire so your team can start internal review.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf, security_questionnaire.pdf

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme-corp.com>, Clara Gomez <clara.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC follow-up: deployment mode & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — yes, that matches our conversation. A few confirmations / details from our side:

1) Deployment mode: Dedicated capacity is our preferred path for the PoC. We want predictable throughput and logical isolation. If the Dedicated PoC demonstrates controls and performance, we will evaluate expanding to a longer-term committed capacity.

2) Stakeholders:
- Bob Lee (SRE lead) — bob.lee@acme-corp.com (technical/network lead for the PoC)
- Clara Gomez (Security) — clara.gomez@acme-corp.com (will run the questionnaire + SOC2 evidences)
- Procurement: I will loop in after the PoC when we land on sizing/pricing.

3) Success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 200ms for our typical 512-token request mix.
- Throughput: sustain 200 rps for 15-minute bursts without queueing beyond 100ms.
- Cost: predictable cost per 1M tokens in line with the quoted dedicated pricing band.
- Quality: model-generated responses meet our rubric with >= 90% acceptable rate on blind eval set (we will share sample prompts).

4) Timeline: Target kickoff next week (w/c Apr 12). PoC duration 3 weeks (kickoff, integration + smoke tests week 1, load testing & tuning week 2, final evaluation week 3).

I've attached the completed security questionnaire (partial answers) — Clara will finish and return any follow-ups.

Best,
Alice
Product Lead, AI Platform
Acme Corp
Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf

Hi Alice / Bob / Clara —

Thanks for the confirmations and the partial questionnaire. Below is a proposed PoC plan aligned to the success criteria and timeline you suggested. I included internal owners from Redwood on the CC.

Proposed PoC (Dedicated capacity) — 3 week plan:
Week 0 (pre-kickoff) — prep
- Exchange network requirements and IP allowlists.
- Obtain sample prompts/eval set from ACME.
- Redwood to reserve a small dedicated pool for testing (Ben).

Week 1 — integration + smoke tests
- ACME integrates calls to the Dedicated endpoint; verify auth/KMS access.
- Smoke test with small volume; validate KV/prefix caching behavior.

Week 2 — load testing & tuning
- Run sustained load profile to validate 200 rps bursts; measure p95 latency.
- Tuning: batching, quantization profile recommendations, autoscale knob settings.

Week 3 — evaluation & handoff
- ACME runs blind eval against sample set for quality.
- Business review: results vs success criteria, recommended next steps (commit / private VPC evaluation).

Success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms across 95% of test windows.
- Throughput: handle 200 rps bursts with <100ms queueing and no error rate increase > 0.5%.
- Quality: >=90% acceptable on ACME's rubric.
- Ops: ability to export audit logs and meet data retention controls per your questionnaire.

Redwood resources:
- Technical lead: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwoodinference.com) — will own infra setup & tuning.
- Solutions: Jordan Blake (jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com) — will coordinate evals and success criteria.

Action items:
- Alice / ACME: confirm kickoff slot (w/c Apr 12), provide SRE + security availability, and share sample prompts by EOD Apr 8.
- Redwood: provide updated PoC timeline and network checklist (attached network_requirements.xlsx).

If that looks good I'll schedule the kickoff and ask Ben to provision the dedicated pool for the week of Apr 12.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: network_requirements.xlsx, redwood-poc-plan.pdf
